subtopics.title: Prove the mid-point theorem and use its converse
subtopics.exposition: Mid-point theorem (parallel part): the line joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side. Mid-point theorem (length part): the line joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is equal to half the length of the third side. A quadrilateral with one pair of opposite sides equal and parallel is a parallelogram (used to show that BCFD is a parallelogram). Converse of the mid-point theorem: if a line is drawn through the mid-point of a side of a triangle parallel to the second side, it will bisect the third side. Investigation: draw a large scalene triangle ABC, find the mid-points D and E of two sides and connect them. Investigation: cut out triangle ABC and cut along DE, place triangle ADE on quadrilateral BDEC (first with E on C, then with D on B), compare the lengths DE and BC, and make a conjecture about the line joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle. Proof of the mid-point theorem, construction: extend DE to F so that EF = DE (by construction), and join C to F. Proof step: from the congruent triangles, angle ADE = angle CFE; these are alternate interior angles, therefore BD is parallel to FC. Proof step: since BCFD is a parallelogram, DE is parallel to BC, so the line joining the two mid-points of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side. Proof step: triangle EAD is congruent to triangle ECF by SAS, because angle E1 = angle E2 (vertically opposite angles), AE = CE (given, E is the mid-point) and DE = EF (by construction). Proof step: BD = DA (given) and DA = FC (from the congruent triangles EAD and ECF), therefore BD = FC. Proof step: use the properties of the parallelogram: opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal, so DF = BC. Proof step: DF = 2(DE) by construction, so 2DE = BC, therefore DE = 1/2 BC.

subtopics.title: Calculate lengths using mid-points
subtopics.exposition: The line joining the mid-points of two sides of a triangle is equal to half the length of the third side (DE = 1/2 BC, equivalently 2DE = BC), so an unknown length can be found from the other.
